messages:
leah: Opening a docs PR to unify function/tool calling examples across SDKs and add a short section on tolerant parsing for streaming outputs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4988 — please skim for link fixes and snippet consistency.

omar: Will do. I'll update Python snippets to `client.call_tool(...)` and add a little pytest showing a repaired parse flow.

jess: For JS, prefer `await redwood.callTool({ name, input })`. Also suggest a tiny async iterator example showing buffering before JSON.parse to handle token-split streams.

leah: Good. Also planning a compact JSON Schema example that uses `oneOf` + `nullable` for optional action payloads and a brief guardrail recommending enums for action types.

docs-bot: link-checker ran on branch — 2 dead example links found, comments posted on PR.

andre: Suggest we include a mini section on diagnostics: show `raw_response` capture, how to log the last 512 chars for reproducible parse failures. Keeps support triage faster.

omar: I'll add that diagnostic snippet to the python example. Draft:
```python
# capture and attempt robust parse
raw = resp.get_text()
try:
    payload = json.loads(raw)
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    log.warn('parse failed', raw[-512:])
    repaired = try_simple_repair(raw)
    payload = json.loads(repaired)
```

jess: JS draft for buffering:
```js
let buffer = '';
for await (const chunk of client.streamTool(...)) {
  buffer += chunk;
}
const obj = JSON.parse(buffer);
```

leah: Nice. I'll also add a one-paragraph note about streaming & parseability: streaming can split tokens (esp. in LLM outputs), so buffer until a complete JSON object is observed or use lenient parsers / repair heuristics.

andre: Could we also add a 1-line test case asserting enum validation fails fast? Helps docs readers understand why explicit enums are better.

omar: Yep — I'll add a pytest that asserts schema validation raises for unknown action string.

docs-bot: formatting/lint checks pending on PR.

leah: Thanks all. Plan: I'll push the link fixes and guardrail paragraph tonight, @omar add python tests, @jess run JS linting. Target merge tomorrow. Any objections?

jess: No objections. I'll watch for followups in the PR and quick patch any style comments. :thumbsup:

omar: Sounds good. I'll also file a follow-up issue to port snippets to the Private docs (VPC/on-prem) after merge.

leah: Perfect — thanks everyone!
